figure: FIGURE A.4 — Where Should Intelligence Live?
issue: The upward red arrowhead is the figure's only directional element and is the most likely source of the 'higher = better / more advanced' reading that the caption explicitly disclaims ('not a ranking of superiority: a lower band is not "better" or "worse" than a higher one'). The caption never explains what the arrow means; its meaning appears only in the small red sub-caption ('scope of placement: intelligence shifts up out of the weights'). The figure therefore asserts a directional trend in its drawing while its caption denies a ranking, and the reader must reconcile two different messages from two different typographic registers.
evidence: Rendered page 452: red arrow with a single upward arrowhead spanning the stack; sub-caption in small red type 'scope of placement: intelligence shifts up out of the weights'; caption 'The horizontal bands are a design choice (which layer owns which capability), not a ranking of superiority…'. The caption contains no reference to the arrow.
acceptance_test: The caption states what the arrow encodes (e.g. 'the arrow marks the historical direction of capability migration, not a ranking'), and the arrow is either labelled in-figure or drawn so it cannot be read as a preference ordering (e.g. double-headed or non-directional connector).

figure: FIGURE A.5 — Shared weights do not remove executed work
issue: In the 'Actual stop' row, a solid flow arrow enters the dashed 'pass 3' box and a second solid arrow leaves it toward 'exit'. The figure's own legend defines 'Solid arrows = flow', so the drawing asserts a flow into a node the figure simultaneously declares 'not executed'. The reader can legitimately infer that pass 3 runs and is then discarded — which is precisely the outcome the caption denies ('A true exit omits later work'). The figure's central distinction is undercut by its own arrow convention.
evidence: Rendered page 459, 'Actual stop' row: pass 1 → pass 2 → [dashed 'pass 3' box, 'not executed' beneath] → [orange 'exit' box]; both connectors appear solid. Legend: 'Dashed arrows = weight reuse; dashed box = not executed' and 'Solid arrows = flow; labeled boxes mark exit / selection'.
acceptance_test: No solid 'flow' arrow enters or leaves the not-executed box. Either the exit arrow runs directly from pass 2 and the dashed 'pass 3 (not executed)' box is placed off the flow path with no connectors, or the connectors into/out of it are dashed and the legend states that dashed connectors also mean 'skipped'. A reader tracing only the arrows cannot conclude that pass 3 executed.

issue: The QLoRA bar (~60 GB) is not reconstructible from the components the note lists, and the bar's own axis label ('weights+adapters') contradicts the arithmetic that would produce 60 GB.
evidence: Note: 'QLoRA: 4-bit (NF4) base + LoRA adapters + a small optimizer.' Recomputation: 70e9 x 0.5 B = 35 GB for the 4-bit base; adapters and optimizer are stated as small, giving ~35-40 GB, not 60 GB. The value 60 GB is reproduced almost exactly by 35 GB (4-bit base) + 24.1 GB (canonical 9.2K FP16 KV, the same 24.1 GB used in the inference bar: 140 + 24.1 = 164.1 ~ 165 GB) = 59.1 GB. So the bar appears to include KV, which the note omits and the bar label excludes. The caption's range '~50-70 GB' is consistent with the bar but not with the note.
acceptance_test: State the composition on the figure (e.g. '4-bit base 35 GB + KV 24 GB + adapters/optimizer ~1 GB') and relabel the bar 'weights + KV + adapters'; or reduce the bar to ~36-40 GB and narrow the caption's range to match. The caption range must bracket the bar's stated composition.

figure: Figure 6.2 (Latency distribution: the mean hides the tail)
issue: The caption attributes the exceedance to a TTFT threshold, but the plotted quantity is request latency; the caveat that this is a superset of TTFT violations lives only in the prose on the previous page, not on the figure or in its caption.
evidence: Figure x-axis: 'Request latency (s)'; shaded band: 'SLO-violating region (> 2 s)'; vertical line: 'SLO 2 s (TTFT budget)'. Caption: '1% of requests exceed the 2 s TTFT threshold'. The prose on PDF 114 / printed 94 states the correct relationship ('Request latency != TTFT, so a TTFT-budget line drawn on request latency flags a superset of TTFT violations'), but the figure sits on the next page and the caption does not carry the caveat. A reader who sees only the figure will read the band as a TTFT violation rate.
acceptance_test: Caption must state that the plotted quantity is request latency and that the 2 s TTFT budget drawn on it flags a superset of TTFT violations; the band label should read '> 2 s (TTFT budget drawn on request latency)'.

issue: The '9.5K' annotation is unexplained in the caption and uses a different canonical context length than Figure 7.6 for the same scenario.
evidence: The annotation '9.5K x 24.9 GB (FP16 bound)' is internally consistent (9,500 x 2.62 MB = 24.9 GB) but the caption never mentions 9.5K or 24.9 GB, and the notation '9.5K x 24.9 GB' reads as a product rather than '9.5K tokens -> 24.9 GB'. Figure 7.6 (PDF 147 / printed 127) states the canonical input as 'max 9.2K canonical input' and derives 24.1 GB of KV there (140 + 24.1 = 164.1 ~ 165 GB). The two figures therefore use different canonical context lengths (9.5K vs 9.2K) for the same canonical scenario, and the house convention fixes 1,200 + 8,000 = 9,200.
acceptance_test: One canonical context length must be used in both figures (9.2K), and the annotation must name what it is (e.g. 'canonical 9.2K-token context -> 24.1 GB FP16 KV'); the caption must reference the annotation explicitly.

issue: A dangling annotation states a per-token rate that the legend already gives for the entire line, at a specific x-position, with no stated consequence and no caption coverage.
evidence: The label '12.6K = 0.33 MB/tok' sits beside the GQA FP16 marker at x ~ 12.6K. The per-token rate 0.33 MB/tok is already in the legend and applies to the whole line, so the annotation conveys nothing on its own. The implied derived quantity is 12.6K x 0.33 MB ~ 4.2 GB, which is never shown. The caption does not mention it.
acceptance_test: Either remove the annotation or restate it as a derived quantity ('12.6K tokens -> 4.2 GB GQA FP16 KV') and add one caption sentence explaining the point being made.

figure: Figure 7.5 (annotations '8x scaling: full-MHA FP16' and '8x scaling: GQA FP16')
issue: Two annotations both labelled '8x scaling' attached to two different curves are self-contradictory on a literal reading and duplicate an unambiguous marker already present.
evidence: The chart carries a clear '8x' label with a vertical double arrow between the red and blue curves near x = 10, which already communicates the ratio. The two longer labels, '8x scaling: full-MHA FP16' (near the red curve at x ~ 100-200) and '8x scaling: GQA FP16' (near the blue curve at x ~ 100), read as if both curves are '8x scaled', which would make their ratio 1 rather than 8. A reader can also misread '8x scaling' as 'scales 8x with context', which is false for every curve (all are linear in context).
acceptance_test: Replace the two labels with a single annotation on the existing vertical arrow, e.g. 'full-MHA FP16 = 8 x GQA FP16 at the same context', and delete the ambiguous pair.

issue: The legend labels the 8-bit full-MHA series as 'FP16', while the parallel 8-bit GQA series is correctly labelled 'FP8'.
evidence: Legend entries: 'full-MHA FP16 (bound, ~2.62 MB/tok)', 'full-MHA FP16 (raw byte-halving, 50%)', 'GQA FP16 (~0.33 MB/tok)', 'GQA FP8 (raw, ~0.16 MB/tok)'. The caption confirms the orange series is the 8-bit curve ('FP16 = 2.62 MB/token, FP8:8-bit = 1.31'). A reader scanning the legend sees two 'full-MHA FP16' series and cannot tell which is 8-bit without reading the caption.
acceptance_test: Rename the entry to 'full-MHA 8-bit (raw byte-halving of FP16, ~1.31 MB/tok)'; no legend entry may label an 8-bit series as FP16.

issue: The y-axis is labelled 'Achievable performance (TFLOPS) — per GPU', but the plotted ceiling is the vendor peak/theoretical datasheet value (the green annotation reads 'compute plateau = 989 TFLOPS'), and the caption explicitly states 'the ceilings are peak/theoretical datasheet values, not achieved runtimes (≈30–40%, 8.5%)'. The axis label therefore asserts the opposite of what the figure plots and what the caption says. A reader who trusts the axis label will read the plateau as a realistic sustained ceiling and will mis-size capacity by roughly 2.5–3×.
evidence: Figure text: y-axis 'Achievable performance (TFLOPS) — per GPU'; plateau annotation 'compute plateau = 989 TFLOPS'; caption 'the ceilings are peak/theoretical datasheet values, not achieved runtimes (≈30–40%, 8.5%)'. 989 TFLOPS is the H100 SXM dense FP16 datasheet peak, not an achieved rate.
acceptance_test: Rename the y-axis to 'Peak (theoretical) performance (TFLOPS) — per GPU' or add '(datasheet peak)' to the axis title, and keep the caption's 'not achieved runtimes' qualifier. Verify that no other figure or table in Ch 8 reuses the phrase 'achievable performance' for a datasheet-peak value.

issue: Two clauses of the caption are not interpretable as printed. (a) 'Convention: a multiply-add counts as 2 FLOPs; the FMA convention of 8,1: dense (no sparsity) FP16' — the token '8,1' is not a meaningful quantity and the sentence has already fixed the convention in its first clause, so the fragment appears to be a corrupted number. (b) 'the plotted prefill (9.2K input) and decode (batch=1) points are illustrative operating points, and a kernel's latency — not measured SLO-goodput.' — the trailing clause has no verb and no predicate; the intended contrast (these are kernel-latency points, not measured SLO-goodput) is not stated. Both are in the caption that is the figure's only interpretive key.
evidence: Caption text as rendered on PDF p.162: 'Convention: a multiply-add counts as 2 FLOPs; the FMA convention of 8,1: dense (no sparsity) FP16; ... and a kernel's latency — not measured SLO-goodput.' Confidence: the characters '8,1' could not be resolved with certainty at 150 dpi (candidates: '8,1', '8:1', '2,1'); the defect is that the clause does not parse under any reading.
acceptance_test: Repair both clauses in the source. Suggested: 'Convention: a multiply-add counts as 2 FLOPs; dense (no sparsity) FP16; the ceilings are peak/theoretical datasheet values, not achieved runtimes (≈30–40%, 8.5%); the plotted prefill and decode points are illustrative kernel-level operating points, not measured SLO-goodput.' Re-read the caption aloud against the rendered page to confirm every clause parses.

issue: The caption says 'decode (batch=1) sits to the left, on the memory-bound slope; and decode (batched=1) sits to the left, on the memory-bound slope and continuous batching climbs the slope as batch grows'. The same predicate ('sits to the left') is applied to two points the figure draws at different positions, and the intended reading ('to the left of the knee') is never stated. The caption also never gives the batch size or the resulting arithmetic intensity for the batched point, so the reader cannot check the plotted marker. The label 'decode (batched=1)' is itself ambiguous — it reads as 'batch = 1' rather than 'batched decode'.
evidence: Recomputed decode intensities for the canonical 70B at FP16: batch=1 → 2·N / (2N + KV) ≈ 1.0 FLOP/byte (weights dominate: 1.4e11 FLOP/token ÷ 1.4e11 B/token), which places the batch=1 marker at 10^0 on the log axis — consistent with the figure's leftmost marker. Batched decode at batch B moves right along the slope (intensity ≈ B for small B), so the batched marker must be to the RIGHT of the batch=1 marker and still left of the 295 ridge for B ≲ 100. The caption's 'climbs the slope as batch grows' is consistent with this, but 'sits to the left' is not.
acceptance_test: Rewrite the caption clause as: 'decode (batch=1, intensity ≈1 FLOP/byte) sits far left on the memory-bound slope; batched decode (batch B, intensity ≈B FLOP/byte) climbs that slope toward the knee, reaching the knee only at B ≈ 295 for H100.' Rename the figure annotation 'decode batched' to 'decode batch B (batched)' and label the plotted batched point with its batch size and intensity so the reader can verify its x-position.

figure: FIGURE 8.1 — Where inference computation and data movement actually live
issue: The legend defines exactly three colour classes — 'compute' (blue), 'memory' (orange), 'interconnect' (green) — but the boxes for 'shared mem (SRAM)' and 'L2 cache' are coloured blue, i.e. classified as compute, although both are memory resources. Only 'HBM (GPU memory)' is orange. The caption then asserts 'compute, memory and interconnect are separate groups within this stack, not levels of one ladder', which the figure's own colour coding contradicts: the reader is shown SRAM and L2 inside the compute group. A reader can legitimately conclude that on-chip SRAM and L2 are compute resources rather than memory, which is exactly the distinction the chapter needs to keep sharp (capacity vs bandwidth vs compute).
evidence: Figure legend (bottom of FIG 8.1): blue = 'compute', orange = 'memory', green = 'interconnect'. Box fills: 'registers', 'tensor cores / ALU', 'shared mem (SRAM)', 'L2 cache' all blue; 'HBM (GPU memory)' orange; 'GPU interconnect', 'other GPUs / remote' green. Caption: 'model weights and the KV cache are predominantly HBM-resident' and 'compute, memory and interconnect are separate groups within this stack'.
acceptance_test: Either (a) add a fourth legend class 'on-chip memory' and recolour the SRAM and L2 boxes accordingly, or (b) relabel the legend as 'on-chip compute / off-chip memory / interconnect' and add one clause to the caption: 'SRAM and L2 are memory resources that happen to be on-chip; they are shown with the compute group because they are on-chip, not because they are compute.' Verify that the caption's 'separate groups' sentence is then literally supported by the colour key.

issue: The legend states 'Solid: data/state flow. Dashed: denoiser conditioning.' But the figure's dashed feedback loop on the right of the 'Wan2.2 dense T2V-5B + scheduler' box is the denoising/scheduler iteration — a control-flow loop, not conditioning — and the caption says so explicitly ('The feedback loop is denoising/scheduler iteration, not architectural recurrence'). A reader applying the legend literally will read the dashed loop as 'conditioning', i.e. as a second conditioning input, which is a different mechanism entirely. The figure therefore uses one visual channel (dash pattern) for two distinct semantic classes.
evidence: Legend line under FIG 8.3: 'Solid: data/state flow. Dashed: denoiser conditioning. Blue: data/state. Orange: compute. Token partitioning adds communication between devices.' Dashed elements in the drawing: (i) UMT5-XXL → denoiser, (ii) VAE encode → denoiser, (iii) the right-hand loop arrow from the denoiser box back into itself. Caption: 'The feedback loop is denoising/scheduler iteration, not architectural recurrence.'
acceptance_test: Give the iteration loop a distinct dash pattern (e.g. dotted, or a dash-dot) and extend the legend to three entries: 'Solid: data/state flow. Dashed: denoiser conditioning. Dotted: scheduler iteration (control flow).' Confirm that after the change no dashed element other than the two conditioning arrows remains.

issue: The caption's parenthetical '(17.5 → 11 at 32K; 436/335 = 1.30 → 1 at 128K)' appears to print '11' as the concurrency at 32K context. By the caption's own stated method — concurrency = 436 GB ÷ KV per request — the 32K figure must be 436 ÷ 84 = 5.19 → 5, not 11. The 128K half of the same parenthetical (436/335 = 1.30 → 1) is correct, which makes the 32K value internally inconsistent with its sibling. If '11' is what is printed, the caption contradicts FIG 7.8's own 'KV 84 GB' bar.
evidence: Recomputed from the figure's own labels: KV per request at 32K = 84 GB (printed in the bar and consistent with 32,000 × 2.62144 MB = 83.84 GB); 436/84 = 5.19 → 5 concurrent. 436/24.9 = 17.51 → 17 (the '17.5' in the same parenthetical). 436/335 = 1.30 → 1 ✓. Confidence: the glyph at 150 dpi could not be resolved with certainty — it may read '5' rather than '11'; the finding is that the value must be checked against the caption's own method.
acceptance_test: Render PDF p.149 at ≥300 dpi and read the 32K concurrency value. It must be 5 (436/84 = 5.19 → 5). If it reads 11, correct it and re-derive the whole parenthetical from the three bar labels (24.9 / 84 / 335 GB) so that all three entries are computed by the same rule.

issue: The caption makes a countable claim the figure cannot support: 'the faint vertical rules inside the KV budget show those 24.9 GB request slots'. Two problems. (a) Legibility: the orange KV region is filled with a regular white dot hatch, and the 'faint vertical rules' are not visually separable from that hatch at print size, so a reader cannot distinguish slot boundaries from fill texture. (b) Counting: 436/24.9 = 17.51 slots is not an integer, so the bar must contain 17 full slots plus a half slot; if the rules are drawn at slot boundaries there will be 18 rules, and counting them yields 18 — the exact wrong answer the caption spends a clause pre-empting ('floor 17, not 18'). The figure thus risks teaching the error it warns against.
evidence: 436 GB ÷ 24.9 GB/request = 17.51. The caption's own text: 'C ≈ 17.5 concurrent (floor 17, not 18; the faint vertical rules inside the KV budget show those 24.9 GB request slots)'. Rendered page: the orange region shows a uniform dot texture; no distinct slot boundaries are resolvable at 150 dpi.
acceptance_test: Make the slot boundaries a distinct, higher-contrast element (e.g. white gaps or a solid 1-pt rule) that is clearly different from the fill hatch, and draw exactly 17 full slots plus one visibly half-width slot, with a small '17 + ½' annotation. Then confirm by counting on a 300-dpi render that the reader obtains 17, not 18. If the rules cannot be made countable, delete the parenthetical claim about the rules and keep the arithmetic in the caption only.

issue: The figure asserts 'in-flight = KV budget ÷ KV per request' and then '→ ~17 requests' with no statement of the operating assumption. The identity only holds if every in-flight request holds the full canonical KV (i.e. every request has run to completion-length context). In a live server, requests at different stages hold different amounts of KV, so 17.5 is a worst-case ceiling on simultaneously-full-length requests, not an expected concurrency. The caption's phrase 'max-FP16 KV' reads as 'maximum precision FP16' and does not carry the worst-case assumption, so a reader can easily take 17.5 as the average concurrency the host will sustain.
evidence: Figure text: 'in-flight = KV budget ÷ KV per request' and '≈ 436 GB ÷ 24.9 GB = 17.5 → ~17 requests'. Caption: 'at 24.9 GB/request max-FP16 KV, C ≈ 17.5 concurrent'. No statement anywhere on the page that each in-flight request is assumed to hold the full 9.5K/9.2K-token KV.
acceptance_test: Add the assumption to the figure itself, e.g. 'in-flight (all at full context) = KV budget ÷ KV per request', and add one clause to the caption: 'this is a worst-case ceiling: it assumes every in-flight request holds the full canonical KV; average concurrency will be higher for shorter requests.' Cross-check that the same assumption is stated wherever 17.5 is reused later in the book.

issue: The operator between '436 GB' and '24.9 GB' in the figure's headline equation renders, at 150 dpi, as a plus sign rather than a division sign: '≈ 436 GB + 24.9 GB = 17.5 → ~17 requests'. If that glyph is genuinely '+', the equation is false (436 + 24.9 = 460.9, not 17.5) and the figure contradicts the line immediately above it ('in-flight = KV budget ÷ KV per request'), which uses a correctly rendered '÷'. The line above proves the author intended division, so the glyph must be checked in the source.
evidence: Rendered page: the line above the equation shows a clear '÷' in 'KV budget ÷ KV per request'; the operator in the equation below does not show the two dots of a '÷' at the same resolution and reads as '+'. Confidence: medium — the glyph is ambiguous at 150 dpi and could be a bold '÷' whose dots were lost in downscaling.
acceptance_test: Render PDF p.148 at ≥300 dpi and confirm the operator is '÷'. If it is '+', replace it with '÷'. Independently, re-set the equation so that the operator is at least as legible as the '÷' in the line above (same weight and size), and confirm that '436 ÷ 24.9 = 17.51 → 17' is what a reader can read off the page without doing arithmetic.

issue: Two caption fragments are not interpretable as printed. (a) 'The fetched implementation uses T_I2V=1/4=1, H_I2V=16, and W_I2V=16.' — 'T_I2V=1/4=1' chains two equalities with no defined quantity; the figure's own box says 'VAE stride (T, H, W) = (4, 16, 16)', so the caption and the figure express the same fact in two incompatible forms. (b) 'For aligned F_φk=1, F_φk+1, F_φk+1=1: 31 latent time positions correspond to 121 frames.' — the subscript sequence appears duplicated ('F_φk+1' twice) and the condition it states is not connected to the 121-frame derivation.
evidence: Caption text as rendered on PDF p.167; figure box text 'VAE stride (T, H, W) = (4, 16, 16)' and 'Aligned endpoint: 1 ? 4 × (31 − 1) = 121 frames'. Confidence: the subscript glyphs could not be resolved with certainty at 150 dpi; the defect is that neither fragment parses.
acceptance_test: Rewrite both fragments so that each quantity is defined once and used consistently with the figure: e.g. 'the fetched implementation uses a temporal compression factor of 4 and spatial factors of 16 (VAE stride (T,H,W) = (4,16,16))' and 'for the aligned first/last-frame factors, 31 latent time positions correspond to 1 + 4 × (31 − 1) = 121 frames'. Confirm the caption and the figure boxes use identical symbols.

page: PDF 177 / printed 157 (legend and caption); also PDF 176 / printed 156 and PDF 181 / printed 161
figure: FIG 9.1 legend, entry 'Two-way HDR: assumed effective 40 GB/s'
issue: The legend label 'Two-way HDR' is ambiguous in a way that changes the answer by 2×, and the same 40 GB/s assumption is given three different names in the book (legend 'Two-way', p.156 'two-rank', p.161 '2 HDR rails/ports per node').
evidence: 'Two-way' most naturally reads as a bidirectional aggregate (send + receive on one link). Under that reading the ring moves 245 GB sent per rank at 20 GB/s per direction = 12.25 s, not the 6.1 s printed in the figure subtitle, the caption, and printed p.156. The book's own framing elsewhere is explicitly per-direction: printed p.161 states '490 GB of sent-plus-received traffic divided by 900 GB/s gives the same time', i.e. 245 GB sent at 450 GB/s directional, and FIG 9.1's NVLink entry is labelled 'directional peak 450 GB/s'. The HDR entry is the only one whose directionality is unspecified, and it is the one whose label admits a 2× misreading.
acceptance_test: Choose one unambiguous descriptor for the 40 GB/s assumption and use it identically in the FIG 9.1 legend, the FIG 9.1 caption, printed p.156, and printed p.161. Recommended: 'HDR, 2 rails/node, assumed effective 40 GB/s per direction'. The words 'per direction' must appear in the legend entry so that the 245 GB / 40 GB/s = 6.125 s arithmetic is forced by the label rather than inferred.

figure: FIG 9.2 subtitle: 'Four ranks; four FP16 elements per input (6 B/rank).'
issue: The parenthetical states the input size as 6 B/rank, but four FP16 elements are 8 B/rank; 6 B is the per-phase sent volume, not the input size. As written the figure's own headline number is wrong.
evidence: Four FP16 elements × 2 B = 8 B per rank of input. The figure body correctly shows '6 B sent + 6 B received/rank' per phase and 'Per rank: 12 B sent + 12 B received = 24 B endpoint total', and the caption says 'each rank sends 12 B and receives 12 B across both phases'. 12 B sent / 8 B input = 1.5 = 2(N−1)/N at N=4, which is the same factor FIG 9.1 uses at N=8 (1.75). If the input really were 6 B, the ratio would be 2.0, contradicting both figures. The parenthetical is attached to 'per input', so the natural reading is input size.
acceptance_test: Rewrite the subtitle as 'Four ranks; four FP16 elements per input (8 B/rank); 6 B sent + 6 B received per rank per phase' and confirm that 8 B input → 12 B sent → 1.5× is stated or derivable on the page. Re-check that no other caption or prose in Chapter 9 repeats the '6 B/rank' input figure.

page: PDF 181 / printed 161 (prose); anchors FIG 9.1 on PDF 177 / printed 157
issue: The prose that supplies FIG 9.1's HDR bandwidth assumption appears to print '200 GB/s per link' where the parenthetical '(= 25 GB/s before link coding)' requires '200 Gb/s'. If the source really reads GB/s, this is an 8× bytes-vs-bits error in the number that anchors the figure's HDR curve.
evidence: Printed p.161: 'HDR InfiniBand delivers 200 GB/s per link (= 25 GB/s before link coding).' 200 Gb/s = 25 GB/s, so the parenthetical is only consistent with 'Gb/s'. The same paragraph then derives 'roughly 40 GB/s (aggregated across 2 HDR rails/ports per node)', i.e. 2 × 25 GB/s × 0.8 efficiency, which is the 40 GB/s used in FIG 9.1's legend and in the 6.1 s ring time. The unit glyph is at the resolution limit of the 150 dpi render, so the source must be checked before acting.
acceptance_test: Open the source for printed p.161 and confirm the unit. If it reads 'GB/s', change to '200 Gb/s per link (= 25 GB/s before link coding)'. If it already reads 'Gb/s', close this finding with no change and record the check. In either case, confirm that the 40 GB/s effective figure in the text matches FIG 9.1's legend entry and that the 2-rail derivation is stated once, not twice.

issue: Panel A's weight bar is drawn as one continuous blue bar split at the GPU boundary and labeled 'W1' (over GPU 0) and 'W2' (over GPU 1). As drawn, the natural reading is 'GPU 0 holds matrix W1, GPU 1 holds matrix W2' — i.e. matrix-per-GPU placement, which is NOT tensor parallelism. Under TP both GPUs hold shards of the SAME matrix. The caption ('TP shards one layer's weights across GPUs') disambiguates in prose, but the figure alone licenses the wrong mental model, and the book elsewhere distinguishes TP from EP ('EP reuses the same machinery'), so the confusion is not harmless.
evidence: Rendered panel A: a single hatched bar spanning both GPU boxes, with 'W1' centered over GPU 0 and 'W2' centered over GPU 1, and no label identifying the parent matrix. Caption: 'TP shards one layer's weights across GPUs (activations replicated; partial sums all-reduced every layer)'. Panel title: 'splits one layer's weights'.
acceptance_test: Panel A's bar must be labeled as one matrix divided into shards — e.g. a brace over the bar reading 'one layer's weight matrix W' with the halves labeled 'shard 1 (GPU 0)' / 'shard 2 (GPU 1)' or 'W[:, :h]' / 'W[:, h:]' — so that no reader can read the drawing as 'GPU 0 holds W1, GPU 1 holds W2'. Re-render and confirm the intended reading is forced by the labels alone, without the caption.

issue: The discrete-batching panel draws four sequences of IDENTICAL length (four equal blue blocks, four equal pink trailing regions). The mechanism the caption and the figure's own annotation describe — 'a batch is locked until its slowest member finishes, so short outputs idle in trailing slots' and 'GPU slots idle (pink) when a sequence finishes early' — requires at least one visibly shorter sequence. As drawn, the picture is equally consistent with the opposite reading: all four sequences ended together and the slots sat idle until the next batch was admitted. The reader therefore cannot see the phenomenon the figure exists to contrast with continuous batching.
evidence: Rendered left panel: four rows, each with an identical short blue block at the left and an identical long pink dotted region to the right, all ending at the same x. Caption: 'In the left (discrete) panel a batch is locked until its slowest member finishes, so short outputs idle in trailing slots'. In-figure annotation: 'GPU slots idle (pink) when a sequence finishes early'. Neither is visible in the drawing.
acceptance_test: In the discrete panel, at least one sequence must be drawn visibly shorter than the others, with that row's pink idle region extending past the other rows' blue regions, so that 'short outputs idle in trailing slots' and 'GPU slots idle (pink) when a sequence finishes early' are both readable from the drawing alone. Confirm at print size that the length difference is unambiguous.

issue: The annotation 'a finishing sequence frees its slot immediately' has a leader arrow whose head lands on an in-flight blue block (or on the green backfill strip), not on the freed slot it names. The freed slot is the white gap between the finished blue block and the backfilled green strip. The arrow therefore points the reader at the wrong element, and the caption's claim that 'freed slots are refilled every step' is not what the arrow demonstrates.
evidence: Rendered right panel, row 2: blue block, then a white gap, then a green strip + blue block. The leader from 'a finishing sequence frees its slot immediately' terminates on the block region to the right of the gap rather than on the gap itself. Legend defines green as 'new sequence (backfill)', so a green target would also mis-name the object.
acceptance_test: The leader from 'a finishing sequence frees its slot immediately' must terminate on the freed slot (the white gap between the finished blue block and the backfilled green strip), or the annotation must be reworded to name the green strip ('a new sequence (green) backfills the freed slot immediately'). Re-render and confirm the arrowhead unambiguously touches the intended element.

issue: Grayscale failure with information loss. 'sequence in flight' is encoded as a solid blue block and 'new sequence (backfill)' as a solid green block — hue is the ONLY distinguishing channel.
